questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A solid metallic cube having total surface area $24 \mathrm{~m}^2$ is uniformly heated. If its temperature is increased by $10^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, calculate the increase in volume of the cube.
$\left(\right.$ Given : $\left.\alpha=5.0 \times 10^{-4}{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}^{-1}\right)$
questions.solution:
We have $\Delta V=V_0 \gamma \Delta T\Delta V=a^3,(3 \alpha) \Delta T$
Now, $6 a^2=24 \quad[\because$ Total surface area of cube $\left.=6 a^2\right]\Rightarrow a^2=4 \Rightarrow a=2$
So, $\Delta V=2^3\left(3 \times 5 \times 10^{-4}\right) \times 10=1200 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~m}^3=1200 \times 10^2 \mathrm{~cm}^3=1.2 \times 10^5 \mathrm{~cm}^3$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A bowl filled with very hot soup cools from $98^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ to $86^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ in 2 minutes when the room temperature is $22^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. How long it will take to cool from $75^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ to $69^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ ?
questions.solution:
The rate of heat flow is given by
$\begin{aligned} \\ & \frac{\Delta Q}{\Delta t}=-K\left(T-T_0\right) \Rightarrow \frac{\Delta Q}{\Delta t}=-K\left(T_{a v g}-T_0\right) \\ \\ & \text { Initially } T_{a v g}=\frac{T_1+T_2}{2} \\ \\ & \text { Here, } T_1=98^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ \\ & T_2=86^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ \end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} & \text { (i) } \frac{\mathrm{ms} \times 12}{2}=-\mathrm{K}\left(\frac{98+86}{2}-22\right) \\ & 6=-\frac{\mathrm{K}}{\mathrm{ms}}\left[\frac{98+86}{2}-22\right] \quad(\because \Delta \mathrm{Q}=\mathrm{ms} \Delta \mathrm{T})\end{aligned}$


Now, cool from $\mathrm{T}_1^{\prime}=75^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$
$\begin{aligned} \\ & \mathrm{T}_2=69^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ \\ & \mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{avg}}=\frac{\mathrm{T}_1^{\prime}+\mathrm{T}_2^{\prime}}{2}=\frac{75+69}{2} \\ \end{aligned}$
(ii) $\frac{\mathrm{ms} \times 6}{\Delta \mathrm{t}}=-\mathrm{K}\left(\frac{75+69}{2}-22\right)$

Divide equation (ii) by (i), we have
$\begin{aligned} \\ & \frac{6}{\Delta t(6)}=\frac{50}{70} \\ \\ & \Delta t=\frac{7}{5}=1.4 \mathrm{~min} \\ \end{aligned}$

questions.q: Steam at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> is passed into <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> of water contained in a calorimoter of water equivalent to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>15</mn><mo> </mo><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> till the temperature of the calorimeter and its contents rises to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>80</mn><mo> </mo><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>. The mass of steam condensed (in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>kg</mi></math> ) is
questions.solution:
(a) According to principle of calorimetry,
heat gained = heat lost
Heat is lost by steam in two stages

(i) Change of state from steam at 100 °C to water at 100 °C is m×540.

(ii) To change water at 100 °C to water at 80 °C is m×1×100-80, where m is the mass of the steam condensed.

Total heat lost by steam is
m×540+m×20=m 540+20=560 m

Heat gained by calorimeter and its contents is
1.1+0.2×80-15=1.12×65 cal 

⇒ 560 m=1.12×65

⇒ m=1.12×65560=0.130 kg

questions.q: Three rods of identical cross-sectional area and made from the same metal, form the sides of an isosceles triangle ABC right angled at B as shown in figure. The point A and B are maintained at temperature T and 2T respectively, in the steady state. Now, assuming that only heat conduction takes place. The temperature of point C will be
questions.solution:
Let T0 be the temperature of point C and x be the length of rod AB or BC.

Then, CA=x2+x2=2x

At steady state, the rate of heat flowing from B to C= rate of heat flowing from C to A.

So, KA2T-T0x=KAT0-T2x

22T-T0=T0-T

By solving, T0=3T(2+1)

questions.q: Two spheres of different materials one with double the radius and one-fourth wall thickness of the other are filled with ice. If the time taken for complete melting of ice in the larger sphere is 25 minute and for smaller one is 16 minute, the ratio of thermal conductivities of the materials of larger spheres to that of smaller sphere is
questions.solution:
Radius of small sphere $=\mathrm{r}$ Thickness of small sphere $=\mathrm{t}$ Radius of bigger sphere $=2 \mathrm{r}$ Thickness of bigger sphere $=\mathrm{t} / 4$ Mass of ice melted $=($ volume of sphere $) \times$ (density of ice) Let $\mathrm{K}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{K}_{2}$ be the thermal conductivities of larger and smaller sphere. 

For bigger sphere, $\frac{K_{1} 4 \pi(2 r)^{2} \times 100}{t / 4}=\frac{\frac{4}{3} \pi(2 r)^{3} \rho L}{25 \times 60}$

For smaller sphere,

$\frac{\mathrm{K}_{2} \times 4 \pi \mathrm{r}^{2} \times 100}{\mathrm{t}}=\frac{\frac{4}{3} \pi(2 \mathrm{r})^{3} \rho \mathrm{L}}{25 \times 60}$

questions.q: A copper sphere cools from $62^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ to $50^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ in 10 minutes and to $42^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ in the next 10 minutes. Calculate the temperature of the surroundings.
questions.solution:
By Newton's law of cooling, $\frac{\theta_{1}-\theta_{2}}{t}=-k\left[\frac{\theta_{1}+\theta_{2}}{2}-\theta_{0}\right]$ ....(1)

A sphere cools from $62^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ to $50^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ in $10 \mathrm{~min}$. $\frac{62-50}{10}=-\mathrm{k}\left[\frac{62+50}{2}-\theta_{0}\right]$ ....(2)
Now, sphere cools from $50^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ to $42^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ in next $10 \mathrm{~min} .$
\frac{50-42}{10}=-\mathrm{k}\left[\frac{50+42}{2}-\theta_{0}\right] ....(3)

Dividing eq $^{\text {n }}$. (2) by (3) we get, $\frac{56-\theta_{0}}{46-\theta_{0}}=\frac{1.2}{0.8}$ or $0.4 \theta_{0}=10.4$
Hence $\theta_{0}=26^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$
